author: Dale Philip
description:
I visited the Glodok area of Jakarta. It was established as a Chinese enclave by the Dutch back in 1740 and to this day remains the largest Chinatown in Indonesia.

In any Chinatown you're always guaranteed to find some good food, so my plan was to enjoy a full day of munching there, breakfast, lunch, dinner, supper and a whole bunch of snacks and desserts as well.

I started off with a Dim Sum breakfast at Pantjoran Tea House and had a lunch less than an hour later at a stall in Gang Gloria.

Gang Gloria is a famous narrow alleyway filled with street food. What caught my eye there was a pork soup called Sekba or Bektim, which uses all parts of the pig, including tongue and nose. It was surprisingly delicious, and was all meat, no carbs, so it didn't ruin my appetite for more food exploration in the Chinatown area.

title: Full Day of Eating in Jakarta's Chinatown 🇮🇩

author: Dale Philip
description: I was exploring Glodok, the large Chinatown area in Jakarta, when a woman was encouraging her child to beg for money from me. This kind of thing is rare in Indonesia, according to my experience travelling in the country, so I was quite shocked.
title: Street Beggars in Chinatown, Jakarta 🇮🇩

author: Dale Philip
description:
Pork Head Soup in Chinatown, Jakarta 🇮🇩

I discovered this delicious pork soup in Glodok, Jakarta which is the biggest Chinatown in Indonesia. There's a famous street food alley called Gang Gloria and that's where I found this tasty dish that's known as Sekba or Bektim.
title: Chinatown Pork Soup

author: Dale Philip
description: I was wandering around Glodok, the biggest Chinatown in Indonesia, when I saw these vendors selling second hand Japanese Manga books printed in Indonesian language. Since I'm trying to learn the language here and they were so cheap, I decided to purchase a handful of them.
title: $0.28 Manga Comic Books on the Streets of Chinatown, Jakarta 🇮🇩
